 Your Black Friday 2026 Shopping Guide: What You Need to Know Before the Big Sale
 Before you fill your cart, here's a rundown of when sales start, which retailers are participating and what to expect this year.
 Sneha Iyer 
 Sneha is a sub-editor turned commerce writer with a love for all things digital.… Read full bio 
 Sneha Iyer
 Read full bio 
 November 10, 2026, 4:25 am ET
 2 min read 
 CNET 
 Black Friday is still a couple of weeks out but we aren’t just sitting around waiting for it. We’ve been tracking deals all month and retailers have already been rolling out early discounts. Don’t worry: You’re not late. There’s plenty of time to map out your purchases before the rush hits. Here’s everything you need to know about Black Friday and Cyber Monday this year to get ready.
 When are Black Friday and Cyber Monday this year?
 Black Friday always lands the day after Thanksgiving, which puts it on Nov. 27 this year, with sales kicking off at midnight. Cyber Monday follows three days later on Nov. 30.
 Which retailers are running sales?
 The usual suspects are in: Amazon, Best Buy, Walmart, Costco and plenty more. Each retailer has its own schedule and here’s when they’re kicking things off:
 More from CNET
 Amazon : Nov. 19-30
 Best Buy : Nov. 19-30
 Walmart : Nov. 12-Dec. 2
 Costco : Nov. 16-30
 While these official dates exist, most retailers are already rolling out deals. And it’s not just the big names anymore. Brands and small businesses are fighting for Black Friday and Cyber Monday shoppers, too, so expect just about every store to have something going on through Nov. 30.
 When do the deals end?
 Black Friday deals don’t always disappear when Black Friday weekend ends. Many retailers carry their promotions into Cyber Monday. You may even find select discounts sticking around into December. That doesn’t mean every deal will last, though.
 Popular products can sell out and prices may change from one day to the next. As the holiday season gets closer, shipping deadlines can also make it harder to get gifts delivered in time.
 Should you wait for Cyber Monday?
 The two events have blurred together and most deals now cover both. The risk of waiting is that the item you’ve been eyeing could sell out in the meantime. Our general advice is to grab a good deal when you see it rather than wait.
 What kind of deals should you expect?
 Pretty much anything you can think of. Whether you’re after a new TV or a pack of paper towels, this is the time to buy. Chances are you’ll find what you need marked down, possibly at its lowest price ever.
 We’re already seeing deals on Apple favorites , laptops , video games and consoles , TVs , headphones and more.
 Is it better to shop online or in person?
 Both can save you money. Online tends to be more convenient and it’s much easier to compare prices across retailers. Many of the biggest discounts are online and some retailers run digital-only promos. Stores still have their place, though, especially for limited-quantity doorbusters or anything you want to get your hands on right away.
